sections.overview: Pseudantechinus woolleyae is a small dasyurid marsupial of arid Western Australia.
sections.identification: It was recognized as a species distinct from P. macdonnellensis in 1988; the two had previously been grouped together.
sections.habitat: It favours rugged, rocky country from the Pilbara south toward the Goldfields.
sections.diet: The sources reviewed do not provide a species-specific prey list.
sections.behavior: Its behavior remains little studied, so no broad activity pattern is asserted here.
sections.reproduction: It is a seasonal breeder; young are born from late July to early October and mature at about seven months.
sections.ecology: Both sexes may be capable of breeding in more than one year, but the available biology rests on a very small sample.
sections.conservation: The Western Australian survey source treats its dependence on rocky ridges and breakaways as a local habitat concern; this is not a global threat category.
